subject: Energy
title: Fusion's Remaining Challenges
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Fusion's Remaining Challenges.

hook.text: Achieving fusion temperatures is only half the battle—containing, sustaining, and harnessing that energy remains hard.

buildup.text: Plasma at 150 million °C destroys most materials—reactor walls must withstand extreme neutron bombardment for years.

discovery.text: Tritium breeding is essential—reactors must produce their own tritium from lithium blankets surrounding the plasma.

twist.text: The world's total tritium supply is only about 25 kg—barely enough for initial fusion experiments, let alone reactors.

climax.text: Building a fusion power plant means solving plasma, materials, breeding, and economics all at once—a huge task.

punchline.text: Physics works—engineering the power plant is the real challenge.

quiz.question: Why must fusion reactors breed their own tritium?
